\boxed{-2(m-1)}

Let $M=\min\limits_{\text{perm }b}\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}b_ib_{i+1}$; the sparkling condition is exactly $M\ge-4$.  
A standard lemma (proved by induction on $m$, the base $m=3$ using $S-M=\max_{i<j}c_ic_j\ge0$) gives for every real $m$-tuple
$$S:=\sum_{1\le p<q\le m}c_pc_q\ge\frac{m-1}{2}\,M.$$
Hence for a sparkling tuple $S\ge\frac{m-1}{2}(-4)=-2(m-1)$.

To see this is best possible, take $(x,-y,\dots,-y)$ with one $x>0$ and $m-1$ copies of $-y$ ($y>0$). Its minimum adjacent sum is $M=y^2-2xy$, attained when $x$ is interior. Imposing $M=-4$ gives $2xy=y^2+4$, and then
$$S=-(m-1)xy+\binom{m-1}{2}y^2=\frac{m-1}{2}\bigl((m-3)y^2-4\bigr)\xrightarrow[y\to0^+]{}-2(m-1).$$
Thus the largest such constant is $T(m)=-2(m-1)$.
